trigger: Lecturer could play but could not understand the situation, ethical purpose and concepts.
diagnosis: Area changes introduced people and consequences before explaining the situation.
Required decisions could precede teaching of the relevant concept.
Clue feedback used abstract conclusions without a concrete application.
Flying controls still used invisible floor-only walking bounds.
changes: 32 authored arrival situations, ethical questions, tasks and specific reflection prompts.
Concrete preparatory evidence objects and teaching in the first two areas.
Existing NPC explanations retained, with a foundational opening question.
Original course explanations available from each activity as contextual expandable reading.
fidelity: Sources remain the original course. Fictional NOVA events illustrate the concepts; they are not historical evidence. Structural coverage and completed clicks do not establish learning equivalence.
limitations: The lecturer has identified substantive comprehension problems. This repair is not a claim that the full experience has demonstrated equivalent or superior learning.
friedmanVerified: Original 1970 text checked: owner/agent responsibility, law and ethical custom, competition without deception or fraud.
